items.note: Published 2023-11-08. Council majority (Greens, SPD, Volt) approved 2.50 EUR first hour and 2.00 per further hour inside Wallring from the coming year, above the administration's proposed 2.00 first-hour unified rate; Oldenburg 2.75, Bielefeld 3.45, Muenster 4.25 for 2 hours are on the page. But the figure '4.50 euros or more' for a 2-hour stay in Osnabrueck is not stated in the article (it is an inference from 2.50+2.00; 'or more' is unsupported).
items.corrected_text: HASEPOST reported that the council majority (Greens, SPD, Volt) approved city-centre garage tariffs from 2024 of 2.50 euros for the first hour and 2.00 euros for each further hour inside the Wallring, above the unified 2.00 euros first-hour rate the administration had proposed. The article says a 2-hour stay would cost 2.75 euros in Oldenburg, 3.45 in Bielefeld and 4.25 in Münster.

items.note: Both Stadtwerke page (published 26.06.2024) and OPG page confirm: from 1 July 2024, 20 new terminals, savings up to 11 percent (two-hour stay), base tariff +50 cents/hour, cashless at most +30 cents. source_title mixes two pages; the given URL is the Stadtwerke page titled 'Per Karte oder Smartphone vergünstigt parken'.
items.corrected_title: Per Karte oder Smartphone vergünstigt parken (Stadtwerke Osnabrück)

items.note: OPG page confirms drivers who cannot find their ticket can type in their plate and the terminal computes time and fee. But it says the trend is toward cashless and 'kuenftig auch ticketlos' (in future also ticketless) parking and that the cashless tariff introduction was brought forward from 2025; 'fully ticketless' / 'moving toward' overstates slightly.
items.corrected_text: The new OPG payment terminals let drivers who cannot find their ticket enter their licence plate, and the machine then works out the parking time and fee. OPG's news item says the trend is towards cashless and, in future, also ticketless parking.

items.note: ZFK article published 2021-01-05: Stadtwerke ended own charging cards at end of 2020, moved customers to NewMotion cards, focus on expanding public charging via subsidiary OPG, 'mehr als 100' public charge points. Title confirmed (with ' | ZFK').

Page states OPG manages over 5,000 parking spaces and about 150 charge points in city and region, at least two to three charge points per garage. Page is undated; the text gives no specific date (date field '2026' is only the research year). Title as given is a descriptor; acceptable.

OPG page dated 26 Aug 2026: phased renovation until 2028, temporary restrictions and changed traffic routing, 'Justizteil' (non-public contract-customer area) fully closed 14.09.2026 to expected early Dec 2026, alternatives Bahnhofsgarage and Ledenhof-Garage. Title exact.
OPG page dated Thursday 1 Oct 2026: parking guidance system not or only partly available 6-9 Oct 2026 due to software changeover (stated as expected), garages remain open. Title exact.
TextilWirtschaft article published 2025-01-07: Muenster investor withdrew from buying the former Galeria building at Neumarkt; building closed October 2020. Title exact.

corrected_summary: Public garage parking in Osnabrück is run by OPG, a Stadtwerke Osnabrück subsidiary, which manages more than 5,000 spaces and about 150 charge points in the city and region. In September 2022 the city said there was no council decision to reduce on-street parking; in December 2022 the council set resident-permit fees of 90 euros from 2023 and 120 euros from 2025, and in November 2023 the council majority approved higher city-centre garage tariffs from 2024. OPG introduced a discounted cashless tariff on 1 July 2024, and a phased renovation of the Kollegienwall-Garage is announced to run until 2028.
